subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Which boundary-semantics direction should OpenClaw land for block-streamed paragraph separators across flush boundaries?
rationale: The remaining choice is not whether the bug exists; it is which of the competing open implementations or metadata-style boundary contract maintainers want to own before merging.

options.title: Consolidate one open PR with overflow proof
options.body: Choose one of the two open candidate PRs, require the maxChars boundary case and real delivered-behavior proof, then close the sibling after the canonical fix lands.

options.title: Require explicit boundary metadata
options.body: Ask contributors to replace text-only separator preservation with explicit boundary metadata through the streaming pipeline before merge.

options.title: Keep issue open and pause both PRs
options.body: Leave the issue as the canonical tracker while maintainers defer the block-streaming boundary contract decision.

recommendation.title: Consolidate one open PR with overflow proof
recommendation.body: Choose one of the two open candidate PRs, require the maxChars boundary case and real delivered-behavior proof, then close the sibling after the canonical fix lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and refined the paragraph block-streaming behavior now under review.
